note: Additive layer on top of brands_to_exclude_final.csv / corrected_brand_decisions.csv — never edits those core Brand Name lists. Each entry's canonicalBrand MUST already exist in brands_to_exclude_final.csv OR brands_to_keep_final.csv (cross-checked on load, fails closed otherwise — widened 2026-08-15 from exclude-only to keep-or-exclude). Adds recognised alternate trading names, confirmed domains, confirmed Companies House group identifiers, and (2026-08-15) an opt-in bareBranchSuffixApproved flag — used only as ADDITIONAL exact-match/anchored-prefix evidence — never a fuzzy/substring match. Where no real, verified domain or company number is known, the array is left empty rather than guessed.

entries.aliasRationale: Real leaked candidate (2026-08-02 audit): 'Nisa Express' (TW15-7765B900) is the same Nisa Group convenience-store retail family as 'Nisa Local', trading under a different exact format name. 'Nisa Corner' (seen in 'Post Office: Nisa Corner', RM2-E01A06D3) is deliberately NOT added here — its brand identity is not independently confirmed, so it is left for review_required rather than auto-excluded, per the instruction not to use unrestricted fuzzy matching.

Greene King's own confirmed pub-format sub-brands (Stonehouse, Sizzling Pubs) are separate, pre-existing entries in brands_to_exclude_final.csv, not aliases of 'Greene King' itself — kept as distinct brand entries since they are how these businesses actually trade, not merely another name for the same string.
entries.companyIdentifierRationale: Greene King plc, Companies House company number 00024694 — public UK company registration data. Enables matching a candidate whose own decisive Companies House record shows this number (or a confirmed subsidiary/group relationship to it) as a Greene King-owned business even where the trading name alone gives no indication. No candidate in the historical dataset was found to carry this number directly (confirmed in the prior read-only audit) — this entry establishes the matching capability for future candidates, not a retroactive claim about existing data.

entries.aliasRationale: Real batch candidate name (2026-08-09 owner chain/group review, documented gap in docs/09_DECISIONS.md): 'Little Waitrose - Cheam' did not match brand 'Waitrose' because 'Little' precedes the brand word with no separator. Registering 'Little Waitrose' as its own multi-word alias reuses the EXISTING multi-word branch-name prefix match (already proven for 'Village Pizza Hounslow') — no new matching logic required. 'Little Waitrose' is Waitrose's own real, recognised smaller-format shop brand, not a guessed variant.

Real batch candidate name (2026-08-09 owner chain/group review, documented gap): 'Southern Co-Op- Banstead Nork Way' did not match brand 'Co-op / Southern Co-operative' — the candidate's own word order ('Southern Co-op...') differs from the registered brand string's ('Co-op / Southern Co-operative'). Registering 'Southern Co-op' (the chain's own real trading name) as an alias reuses the existing multi-word prefix match; normalisation already collapses the hyphen/case variants ('Co-Op' vs 'Co-op'), so no separate punctuation handling was needed. 'Southern Co-operative' added alongside for the fully-spelled-out form.
No alias needed — see bareBranchSuffixApproved below.
entries.bareBranchSuffixRationale: Real batch candidate name (2026-08-09 owner chain/group review, PRE-EXISTING gap — Londis was already an EXCLUDE brand before this session's changes): 'Londis Beddington Gardens' did not match brand 'Londis' — single-word brand directly followed by a branch/location phrase with a bare space, no separator character at all. 'Londis' is a distinctive registered convenience-store fascia name, not a generic word — opting it in to the bare-branch-suffix match carries none of the Phoenix/Premier/Flames coincidental-overlap risk the single-word exact-match default exists to prevent.

'Aksular' is a distinctive registered brand name, not a generic word — safe to opt in.
